deck: Table Rock and Taneycomo, written like a fishing magazine — two waters, one week, nothing invented on the outdoor desk.

play.title: Find the shad, not the bank.
play.body: If the graph is empty, keep moving. Late August bass live on bait schools in 15–35 feet. A flutter spoon through them is the grown-up play.

season.name: Dog days
season.why: This is the hard season on the White River system, and it is also when the fishermen who live here quietly catch fish. Thermocline is set. Shad are deep. Table Rock surface is in the 80s. Taneycomo is still 50-degree tailwater.
tips: Fish the first 45 minutes like it matters. After that, put the topwater away.
Table Rock: 15–35 feet, electronics on. You are looking for bait, not banks.
Taneycomo: two- to six-pound test, pink Power Worm, no hero hookset.
MDC wants spotted bass harvested on Table Rock. Keep the spots. Put the 12-to-20-inch rainbows back.
Noon in August is not a fishing hour. Night on the points is a different lake.
License 16–64, plus a trout permit for Taneycomo. Bass Pro at the Landing sells both.

body: Warm surface water around 78°F, clear conditions, and the ongoing drawdown have pushed bass, walleye, and crappie tighter to deeper main-lake structure. Fish are holding on offshore rock piles, brush, roll-offs, and channel swings in the 15–25 ft range. Football jigs are producing quality bass (including solid smallmouth reports) while drop-shots and Neds get the numbers; covering water with good electronics separates the successful trips from the slow ones. Low-light topwater remains effective around points and creek-arm backs, and schooling activity still pops periodically on humps. Walleye continue productive on gravel points with live bait or finesse presentations. Crappie relate to deeper timber. Recent trips report strong jig bites and 20–40+ bass days possible when conditions align. It's a technical grind that rewards preparation and mobility as we edge closer to fall turnover — m

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~20 cfs at 09:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: The cold, clear tailwater fishery remains in solid late-summer form per John Sappington's September 2026 overview and recent Lilleys' Landing patterns. Low morning flows (typical overnight minimums) create the best windows for wading anglers and dock fishermen from just below the dam downstream. When generation ramps in the afternoon and evening, shift to boat drifts targeting current seams, breaks, eddies, and deeper holding water. Pink Power Worms have been the standout bait, often fished on a split-shot rig or under a float, alongside micro jigs, midges, scuds, eggs, and nightcrawlers. Light line and clean presentations are essential in the gin-clear water — rainbows make up the bulk of catches with some larger fish (17–23") and occasional browns possible. ## Why open this tomorrow Overnight shifts in the SWPA generation schedule, any early-September cool front, rainfall in the White River basin, or continued lake-level movement could reposition fish or open new bite windows on both waters. Taneycomo tactics flip the instant the turbines start or stop, while Table Rock offshore patterns often sharpen with small changes in clarity or temperature as fall approaches. Check tablerocklakelevel.com, the USACE gage, and the SWPA hotline first thing — tomorrow could reward a completely different timing or presentation than today.

## Desk note Levels and generation drawn from tablerocklakelevel.com (evening 9/9 readings ~912.8 ft with turbine flows swinging 6k–12.5k cfs, 0 spill) and RiverApp/USGS confirmation (~912.82 ft at dam, ~56.3°F at School of the Ozarks). Taneycomo tactics and patterns carried from John Sappington September 2026 overview (low overnight/early flows, pink worms/micro jigs/split-shot, dock timing during light water), Lilleys' patterns, and recent FishingBooker reports (strong rainbow counts on split-shot, quality bass on jigs).
